passages.text: Photosynthesis is the process plants use to make their own food. It takes place mainly in the leaves, inside green parts of the cells called chloroplasts. These contain chlorophyll, a green substance that absorbs energy from sunlight. The plant takes in carbon dioxide from the air through tiny holes called stomata, and absorbs water from the soil through its roots. Using light energy, it turns these into glucose, a sugar, and releases oxygen as a by-product. The word equation is: carbon dioxide + water, in the presence of light, makes glucose + oxygen.

A food chain shows how energy passes from one living thing to another. Every food chain begins with a producer, which is a green plant that makes its own food using sunlight. Animals that eat plants are called primary consumers, or herbivores. Animals that eat other animals are secondary or tertiary consumers, or carnivores. In the chain grass, then rabbit, then fox, the grass is the producer, the rabbit is the primary consumer and the fox is the secondary consumer. Arrows point in the direction energy flows. Decomposers, such as fungi, break down dead matter and return nutrients to the soil.

All living things are made of cells, the tiny building blocks of life. Animal cells have a nucleus, cytoplasm, a cell membrane and mitochondria. The nucleus controls the activities of the cell. Cytoplasm is the jelly-like liquid where chemical reactions happen. The cell membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell. Mitochondria release energy from food. Plant cells have all of these parts and also have a cell wall made of cellulose for support, a large vacuole filled with sap, and chloroplasts for photosynthesis. Most cells are too small to see without a microscope.

Digestion is the breakdown of large pieces of food into small molecules the body can absorb. It starts in the mouth, where teeth chew the food and saliva begins to break down starch. The food travels down the oesophagus to the stomach, where acid and enzymes break down proteins. In the small intestine, digested food passes through the walls into the blood. The large intestine absorbs water from what is left. The remaining waste leaves the body through the anus. The liver makes bile, which helps to digest fats.

Matter exists in three main states: solid, liquid and gas. In a solid, the particles are packed tightly in fixed positions and can only vibrate, so a solid keeps its shape. In a liquid, the particles are close together but can slide past each other, so a liquid flows and takes the shape of its container. In a gas, the particles are far apart and move quickly in all directions, so a gas fills any container. Melting changes a solid to a liquid, boiling changes a liquid to a gas, and condensing changes a gas back to a liquid.

The water cycle describes how water moves around the Earth. The heat of the Sun makes water in oceans, lakes and rivers evaporate and rise into the air as water vapour. Plants also lose water vapour through their leaves, which is called transpiration. High in the sky the air is cold, so the vapour condenses into tiny droplets that form clouds. When the droplets grow heavy, they fall as precipitation, such as rain, snow or hail. The water then runs into rivers and seeps into the ground, and eventually returns to the sea so the cycle can begin again.

A force is a push or a pull, measured in newtons (N). Forces can change the speed, direction or shape of an object. Friction is a force that acts between two surfaces that rub together and it always opposes motion. Rough surfaces, such as sandpaper, create a lot of friction, while smooth or oily surfaces create less. Friction is useful because it lets shoes grip the ground and brakes slow down a bike. However, it also wastes energy as heat and causes wear on moving parts, which is why machines are often lubricated with oil.

A magnet is an object that attracts certain metals, such as iron, nickel and cobalt. Every magnet has two poles, called the north pole and the south pole. The strongest magnetic force is at the poles. Opposite poles attract each other, while like poles repel each other. So two north poles pushed together will move apart. The area around a magnet where its force can be felt is called its magnetic field. Materials such as plastic, wood and aluminium are not attracted to magnets. A compass needle is a small magnet that lines up with the Earth's magnetic field.

An electric circuit is a complete loop that lets electric current flow. A simple circuit needs a power source, such as a cell or battery, wires to carry the current, and a component such as a bulb. If there is a gap anywhere in the loop, the current stops, so a switch works by opening and closing a gap. Materials that let current pass easily, such as copper, are conductors. Materials that do not, such as rubber and plastic, are insulators. In a series circuit there is only one path for the current, while in a parallel circuit there are several branches.

The solar system is made up of the Sun and everything that travels around it. There are eight planets. In order from the Sun they are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. The four inner planets are small and rocky, while Jupiter and Saturn are giant planets made mostly of gas. Earth takes one year, about 365 days, to orbit the Sun, and it spins once on its axis every 24 hours, which gives us day and night. The Moon is a natural satellite that orbits the Earth about once every month.
